other.recommendation_rationale: 4 images with no human annotations and 6 balls; not enough to reason about.

plain_A.recommendation_rationale: Standard broadcast, the cleanest run: 2.2% missed-role, 1.4% U. Its ball value is modest (12 balls <=8px) but its annotations are the most trustworthy here.

plain_B.recommendation_rationale: Standard broadcast and the largest clean run: 555 images, 464 balls, 65 at <=8px, 3.5% missed-role. Good value at acceptable risk.

pp_A.recommendation_rationale: High/wide tactical, only 49 images, and the worst U rate (2.8%) with a 12.8% missed-role rate. It carries 40 balls <=8px, which is real value for its size, so it is not worth discarding outright -- but it is too small and too noisy to take whole without the retrospective role review.
pp_A.conditional_on: retrospective MISSED_ROLE_REVIEW completed for this run

pp_B.recommendation_rationale: The decisive run, and the uncomfortable one. It is 35.4% of images but supplies 357 of the 474 balls at <=8px -- 75% of the entire tiny-ball value that made keremberke worth repairing. It is also the worst annotated: a 16.2% missed-role rate and 3,288 boxes in the retrospective queue. EXCLUDING it would remove the reason to use this dataset at all, so it is KEEP -- but strictly CONDITIONAL on the retrospective role review being completed for this run first.
pp_B.conditional_on: retrospective MISSED_ROLE_REVIEW completed for this run

camera_type_rule: HIGH_WIDE_TACTICAL when a frame carries >=16 annotated humans AND the median human is under 7.5% of frame height; measured, not eyeballed

high_wide_question.question: does the high/wide tactical run cost more than it gives?
high_wide_question.answer: BOTH, and that is the finding -- it is simultaneously the main source of annotation trouble and the main source of the value.
high_wide_question.conclusion: Excluding the pp runs removes 84% of the balls at <=8px and 99% of those at <=5px. Since tiny broadcast balls were the entire reason keremberke ranked above every other audited source, exclusion would leave a dataset with no advantage over what EyeCU already has. The cost must be paid by finishing the role review, not by dropping the run.
